title: Structural chemistry of the cleavage faces of compound semiconductors
abstract: The major features of the reconstructed atomic geometries of the (110) surfaces of zincblende structure compound semiconductors are characterized by two parameters: the relative displacement perpendicular to the surface of the anions and cations in the outermost layer Δ1,⊥ and the angle ω1 between the plane determined by the chains of these species in the reconstructed surface and the truncated bulk surface. Analysis of the surface sructures of nine compound semiconductors reveals a linear correlation between Δ1,⊥ and the bulk cubic lattice constant a0. A linear correlation between ω1 and a0 also is suggested, but is less firmly established. If the sum of either the Pauling covalent radii or the nonlocal pseudopotential core radii are substituted in place of a0 comparable correlations are achieved. The structures of two previously unexamined surfaces, InAs(110) and AlP(110), are shown to be predicted correctly by these correlations.
